sites.name: Fudge Site
sites.summary: A 31-acre earthwork rectangle that James McBride surveyed in 1847. The walls have been plowed down, and the 9 ft central mound was dug out in the late 1920s.
notes: The relief shows two parallel raised bands 320 m apart. The north one stands about 0.45 m above the ground 25 m to either side, the south one about 0.3 m. The plate puts the walls 1080 ft (329 m) apart.
Fitting the plate's walls to the relief gives 0.47 m per plate pixel, within 2% of the plate's own labeled sizes.
A county road now crosses the north third of the enclosure. A quarry lake sits where the southern half of the east wall should be.

plate.source: Squier & Davis 1848, Plate XXXIII No. 2 (surveyed by James McBride, 1847). Scan: Internet Archive ancientmonuments00squi leaf n203.
plate.label: Plate XXXIII No. 2

sites.name: Hopeton Works
sites.summary: A 20-acre circle joined to a 20-acre square, with parallel walls running 2400 ft toward the Scioto. Squier and Davis surveyed it in 1846. It is now part of Hopewell Culture National Historical Park.
notes: The circle and the square both show as low rises in the relief. The circle is about 300 m across, close to the plate's 1050 ft (320 m).

The plate draws the square about 15% smaller than its own 900 ft label, so no single rotation and scale fits both shapes. The fit follows the circle; the real square extends past the drawn one to the south and west.
The plate is rotated about 34 degrees from page-up to true north.

plate.source: Squier & Davis 1848, Plate XVII (surveyed by E. G. Squier and E. H. Davis, 1846). Scan: Internet Archive ancientmonuments00squi leaf n129.
plate.label: Plate XVII
